reason: E1 shows that a dense nanocrystalline glaze layer forms on a different alloy (Ni50(AlNbTiV)50) at 800 °C and reduces wear, supporting the first two premises. However, no cited evidence supports the premise that annealing FeNiCrCoCu at 800 °C will form such a layer, as E2 discusses a different alloy system and does not address glaze layer formation.
premises: A dense nanocrystalline glaze layer can form on certain alloys during high-temperature wear.
Such a glaze layer minimizes adhesive and oxidative wear.
Annealing at 800 °C can promote the formation of this glaze layer in FeNiCrCoCu.
